purpose: Extend the prior CPU-only execution ceiling to the specifically bounded synthetic GPU qualification; retain all prior mechanism, privacy, recovery and claim limits.

prior_review.reuse_basis: Same source, frozen configuration, tests, mechanism and lifecycle contract; only the authorized execution hardware has become available. No new external review was attempted or attributed.

hardware_context.authority: Parent reports existing project gpu-training authorization for gpushare-i1-54996-titan5
hardware_context.gpu: Two GTX TITAN X cards, 12 GiB each
hardware_context.compatibility: Parent reports CUDA available and sm50 supported by this installed build
hardware_context.gpu_test_status: NOT_RUN_BY_REVIEWER; production GPU execution and acceptance remain pending

synthetic_gpu_canary.profile: synthetic_canary only; frozen public synthetic fixture
synthetic_gpu_canary.initial_topology: --gpu auto, restricted to the two authorized visible Titan devices; one worker per selected GPU
synthetic_gpu_canary.fixed_controls: disabled and random_phase have zero optimizer updates; do not invent six updates for fixed controls
synthetic_gpu_canary.lifecycle: Use the real parent-to-child launcher with --inject-oom-once and --stop-after 2; expect a durable safe-pause result. Resume the same immutable run on one authorized visible GPU, with --canary retained and the stop limit removed. Use CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to constrain auto selection, never change scientific configuration.
synthetic_gpu_canary.parallelism_meaning: Independent per-selector queue scheduling across GPUs; this is not DDP or a single selector spanning two cards
synthetic_gpu_canary.network_publication: Canary must not upload, export a formal report, commit or push; its existing code path already skips formal finish()

isolated_real_allocator_oom_probe.scope: One temporary standalone process on one authorized visible GPU, executed separately from the canary
isolated_real_allocator_oom_probe.method: Record its own small-allocation baseline, attempt one tensor allocation whose bytes exceed that device's total physical memory, and catch only torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError as the expected result. Do not ramp allocations toward the free-memory boundary or hold a near-capacity tensor.
isolated_real_allocator_oom_probe.recovery: Drop only this process's references, optionally empty only its allocator cache, and verify a small CUDA allocation/operation and synchronization still succeed. Exit the probe and check its GPU process/context is gone.
isolated_real_allocator_oom_probe.limits: No allocation loop, no retry ladder, no hardware reset, no cache clearing for other processes, no termination or suspension of other users' processes
isolated_real_allocator_oom_probe.evidence_limit: This proves a real allocator OOM is classified and this temporary process recovers/releases its own context. The launcher canary separately proves injected-OOM recovery. Combining those observations does not establish an actual training-step CUDA OOM has passed the entire worker recovery path.

real_data_gpu_probe.reason: Not part of the requested run. Any later probe requires the planned authorized data transfer and a separate explicit bounded execution decision; no real data should be copied or processed under this addendum.

pre_execution_conditions: Resolve the registered authorized Titan host and exact environment through the project server authority; do not substitute the collaborator's inaccessible server.
Confirm the transferred checkout matches the reviewed manifest and source commit before starting. Any source/config/test change invalidates reuse until reviewed.

Recheck both devices and their supported CUDA capability in the selected environment, and preserve existing CUDA visibility restrictions. Each selected device must pass the runner's existing >=8 GiB free gate.
Use a fresh synthetic run directory; retain its original fingerprint during one-GPU resume. Do not edit memory tiers, counts, budgets or selectors to make a check pass.
Use bounded timeouts and terminate only the spawned canary's own process groups if cleanup is required. Record an ordinary failure rather than assuming every CUDA error is an OOM.
required_acceptance_evidence: GPU inventory, selected physical UUIDs, environment versions, reviewed source manifest hash and exact launch/resume commands, without credentials.
Actual child processes using isolated CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, baseline dependency completion, and simultaneous independent selector activity across both GPUs when the queue permits.
Expected injected OOM classification, exactly persisted tier advancement, safe pause at a complete optimizer boundary, and successful same-run one-GPU resume retaining the tier and completed jobs.

All eight jobs complete with strict full-value trace validation, finite gradients, actual CUDA memory telemetry and unchanged scientific fingerprint. Record runtime and memory as tiny-canary measurements, not full Re-TACRED speed estimates.
Independent allocator probe catches the actual expected CUDA OOM, successfully performs a small post-error operation, and exits without leaving its GPU context or touching other processes.
Retain raw local diagnostic logs and bounded machine-readable summaries; no formal readiness claim is made before the resulting checks are inspected.

remaining_risks: Complex matrix exponential/backward and the original-QK path have not yet been measured on these older sm50 GPUs; the bounded canary is specifically intended to expose kernel, numerical or architecture issues.
Synthetic short-sequence success cannot certify long real sequences, full-data peak memory, throughput, real training OOM recovery or model quality.
CUDA floating-point execution need not be bitwise equal to CPU or a different GPU; use finite-value and declared numeric-tolerance checks rather than claiming cross-hardware bitwise reproducibility.
Private portal import, full formal experiment readiness and report publication acceptance remain independent outstanding work.

execution_ceiling: Specifically the synthetic two-GPU launcher canary, safe one-GPU same-run recovery, and one standalone above-total-memory allocator probe described here. No full-data training, release, publishing, unrelated process manipulation, or optional real-data GPU probe.
